name: AMD Instinct MI455X
disclaimer: MI455X was unveiled at AMD's Advancing AI 2026 event for the Helios rack platform; it is not yet shipping. Figures below are AMD's announced specs. Die counts, cache size and fabric bandwidth come from AMD's own disclosure plus press coverage of the reveal; exact die sizes, floorplan and packaging process were not published, so all geometry/layout is illustrative and marked estimate.

components.name: Package substrate
components.desc: Multi-die organic substrate carrying 12 chiplets (8 compute, 2 fabric/cache, 2 I/O) and 12 HBM4 stacks. AMD has not published package dimensions or the exact advanced-packaging process used.

components.name: Silicon interposer / bridges
components.desc: Carries the fine die-to-die wiring between XCD compute chiplets, the two fabric/cache dies, the I/O dies and the HBM4 stacks. AMD has not disclosed whether this is CoWoS-style silicon bridges, a full interposer, or hybrid bonding directly between dies (MI300-series used TSMC SoIC 3D stacking for some layers) — packaging approach is an estimate.

specs.label: Packaging
specs.value: Multi-die chiplet package (exact process not disclosed)

components.name: I/O die (left)
components.desc: One of two I/O dies. Terminates external links: UALink-over-Ethernet scale-up to the rest of the Helios rack, Infinity Fabric to the host EPYC CPU, and PCIe Gen6 / AMD AI-NIC scale-out.

components.name: I/O die (right)
components.desc: Second I/O die, mirrors iod-left.

components.name: UALink-over-Ethernet (scale-up)
components.desc: 72 UALoE (UALink-over-Ethernet) lanes give GPU-to-GPU scale-up bandwidth across the Helios rack, independent of PCIe/NIC scale-out links.

components.name: Infinity Fabric (host link)
components.desc: Coherent Infinity Fabric link to the host AMD EPYC (Venice) CPU; separate from the UALink scale-up fabric and from PCIe/NIC scale-out.

components.name: Fabric + Cache die (left)
components.desc: One of two Fabric-and-Cache Dies (FCD, TSMC N3P). Each FCD hosts shared L2 cache, the memory controllers for 6 HBM4 stacks, and the die-to-die fabric that the 4 XCD compute chiplets stacked above it use to reach memory and each other. CDNA 5 removes the separate 256 MB Infinity Cache of prior generations and folds its role into this larger, faster L2.

components.name: Fabric + Cache die (right)
components.desc: Second Fabric-and-Cache Die, mirrors fcd-left, serving the other 4 XCDs and 6 HBM4 stacks.

components.name: L2 cache (left FCD)
components.desc: Shared L2 slice on this FCD, visible to the 4 XCDs stacked above it. Replaces the old per-XCD 4 MB L2 + chip-wide 256 MB Infinity Cache with one larger, unified cache tier.

components.name: L2 cache (right FCD)
components.desc: Shared L2 slice on the right FCD.

components.name: HBM4 base die (left group)
components.desc: Logic base die of each HBM4 stack feeding the left FCD. 6 stacks per side, 12 total.

components.name: HBM4 DRAM layers (left group)
components.desc: Stacked HBM4 DRAM dies (announced 432 GB total across 12 stacks; HBM4 doubles the per-stack interface to a 2,048-bit bus vs HBM3e). Layer count per stack not disclosed, drawn as 8 for symmetry with other models.

components.name: HBM4 base die (right group)
components.desc: Logic base dies of the 6 HBM4 stacks feeding the right FCD.

components.name: HBM4 DRAM layers (right group)
components.desc: Stacked HBM4 DRAM dies feeding the right FCD and its 4 XCDs.

components.name: XCD compute chiplets
components.desc: 8 Accelerator Complex Dies (XCD, TSMC N2), 4 stacked logically above each FCD (real packaging likely 3D-stacks XCDs on top of the FCD base die, as MI300-series did; this model draws them side by side for clarity). Each XCD holds 2 shader engines of CDNA 5 Compute Units plus the WGP front ends. Click **Open** to look inside.

components.name: WGPs (Work Group Processors)
components.desc: Each XCD packs 2 shader engines × (16 active + 2 redundant) WGPs = 36 WGPs, of which 32 are active (256 active WGPs across the 8 XCDs on the package). Each WGP pairs 2 Wave32 Compute Units sharing one 384 KB LDS block. Grid is symbolic — exact floorplan not disclosed. Click **Open WGP** to look inside.

components.name: LDS (Local Data Share)
components.desc: 384 KB Local Data Share shared by the 2 Wave32 Compute Units of a WGP. CDNA 5 removes the separate per-CU L1 cache seen in earlier generations, leaning more on this scratchpad plus the larger shared L2 on the FCD below.

components.name: Matrix Core
components.desc: AMD's matrix-multiply units (the CDNA equivalent of Tensor Cores). CDNA 5 widens MXFP4/MXFP6/MXFP8 throughput up to 4× generation-over-generation, which is most of the 40 PFLOPS FP4 figure. A wavefront issues the MFMA instruction; operands stream from the LDS.

components.name: Vector register file
components.desc: Per-wavefront vector registers feeding the Matrix Cores and scalar ALUs. One slice per Compute Unit.

components.name: Wavefront scheduler + ALUs
components.desc: Issues one Wave32 wavefront (32 threads) per cycle to the Compute Unit's ALUs and Matrix Cores; runs the epilogue (bias add, activation, requantize) after the MFMA result lands.

steps.text: 1. Weights W and activations X sit in HBM4, 6 stacks per side.
2. The memory controller on the nearest Fabric + Cache Die (FCD) reads its 6 attached HBM4 stacks.
3. If the needed tile lives on the other FCD's memory, it crosses the inter-die fabric between the two FCDs.
4. Data lands in the shared L2 on that FCD — CDNA 5 folds the old Infinity Cache into this larger, unified cache.
5. The 4 XCDs stacked above this FCD pull their tile from L2 into the LDS of the active WGP.
6. A and B tiles sit in the 384 KB LDS shared by the WGP's 2 Compute Units, ready for the Matrix Cores.
7. The wavefront scheduler issues an MFMA instruction; Matrix Cores multiply the tiles (e.g. in MXFP4).
8. Partial sums accumulate across passes along K, held in the vector register file.
9. Epilogue: the scheduler's ALUs add bias, apply activation, requantize the result.
10. Results flow back through L2 to HBM4; across GPUs, UALink-over-Ethernet (3.6 TB/s) carries the all-reduce for tensor/expert parallelism around the Helios rack.

summary.value: TSMC N2 (XCD compute chiplets), N3P (fabric/cache dies)
256 CUs (128 active WGPs x 2 CUs; 16 WGPs per XCD x 8 XCDs)
20 PFLOPS FP8 / FP6 (announced peak), per GPU
5,000 TFLOPS FP16 / BF16 matrix (5 PFLOPS announced), per GPU
~192 MB L2 (2 x 96 MB on fabric/cache dies; Infinity Cache removed); excludes LDS and register files
192 MB combined (96 MB per FCD, shared by 4 XCDs each)
3,600 GB/s bidirectional UALink-over-Ethernet (72 lanes), per GPU
256 GB/s Infinity Fabric host link to the CPU
12-die chiplet package (exact advanced-packaging process not disclosed)

scale.basis: No official die, stack or package dimensions disclosed by AMD; proportions are illustrative only, loosely following MI300-series precedent for relative chiplet/HBM sizing.
